page.layout: One column of running text; no margin notes; catchword at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: mento ordinis, sive sacerdotii; verum cum non liceat, ut probe scis, in ea Bibliotheca quantum libuerit immorari, brevitate temporis coactus nonnulla passim praetermisi, quæ scopo meo videbantur mihi minus[?] prodesse, ea nunc operâ & ductu tuo resarcire & complere vellem, ut illius libri editio, quam meditor, perfectior, sit & cumulatior. R. Pater Anthonius Petit, qui has literas tibi tradidit, quæcunque erunt necessaria, & jusseris Amanuensi, persolvet.

Rogo tantum, ut autoritate tua descriptionis jus obtineas, Amanuensemque, qui scribere sciat Græce, eligas atque quæ scribenda sunt, prærnonstres; ut hoc commode & minimo cum labore fieri possit: quæ excripsi & quæ prætermisi in tabella huic Epistolæ conjuncta, adnoto & velut depingo: hoc insuper te rogo, ut considerato scopo & opere meo, si qua in re illud juvare potes, cum in commodum Græcorum, quorum mores sacros illustrare laboro, mihi non deneges, jam multorum debitor sum, plu-

page.notes: The word "minus" is partly obscured by a blot over the "n"; read as "minus" with [?]. The word "præmonstres" is printed with a damaged letter that I read as "præmonstres"; the first letters are partly unclear, so the reading is marked as doubtful in the text. The final word "plurium" is split: "plu-" ends the text, and "rium" stands as the catchword at the right. The running head is set in small capitals and is copied as "Petrus à Valle".
